A planned six-day ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump and tied to a humanitarian aid mission in a Russian-occupied town has brought rare quiet to the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson.
The pause in fighting is aimed at paving the way for humanitarian relief for Oleshky, where residents face acute shortages of food and medicine. The ceasefire was initially slated to begin Oct. 29, but the two sides moved the startup by two days, with the guns falling silent at 4 a.m. Moscow time Tuesday.
Ukraine said on Wednesday that the six-day ceasefire, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, was holding.
